questions.prompt: A circle is centered at the origin and contains the point (0, 2). Prove or disprove that the point (1, √3) lies on the circle.
questions.prompt_markup: A circle is centered at the origin and contains the point (0, 2). Prove or disprove that the point (1, √3) lies on the circle.
questions.correct_answer: Proved: the radius is 2 and the distance to (1, √3) is √(1 + 3) = 2.
questions.required_method: Find the radius, then compare the distance from the origin to (1, √3).
questions.grading_note: Any valid coordinate proof. Essential: radius 2; distance √(1² + (√3)²) = 2; conclusion.

branch.new_demand: Prove circle statements for every point using variables (Thales' theorem by slopes).

questions.domain: Geometry: Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations
questions.skill: Coordinate proofs about circles with variables
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: A(-r, 0) and B(r, 0) are endpoints of a diameter of the circle x² + y² = r², and P(x, y) is any other point on the circle. Prove that ∠APB is a right angle.
questions.prompt_markup: A(-r, 0) and B(r, 0) are endpoints of a diameter of the circle x² + y² = r², and P(x, y) is any other point on the circle. Prove that ∠APB is a right angle.
questions.correct_answer: slope PA · slope PB = y²/(x² - r²) = y²/(-y²) = -1, so PA ⊥ PB.
questions.required_method: Compute the slopes of PA and PB and use x² + y² = r².
questions.grading_note: Any valid coordinate proof. Essential: slopes y/(x + r) and y/(x - r); product y²/(x² - r²); substitute x² - r² = -y²; product -1. (P is not A or B, so y ≠ 0.)
